A 25-year-old male arrives at the emergency department after his girlfriend noticed a change in his skin
color following a long morning hike. His medical history includes asthma and substance use
(marijuana, IV drugs, and alcohol). He takes albuterol, fluticasone, and ibuprofen. His vital signs show:
temperature 98.8°F (36.4°C), blood pressure 112/66 mmHg, pulse 62/min, respirations 8/min, and
oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Laboratory results reveal: Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL Hematocrit: 32%
Leukocyte count: 5,500 cells/mm^3 (normal differential) Platelet count: 207,000/mm^3 Serum studies: -
Na+: 139 mEq/L - Cl-: 99 mEq/L - K+: 4.3 mEq/L - HCO3-: 24 mEq/L - BUN: 17 mg/dL - Glucose: 89
mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL - Ca2+: 10.1 mg/dL - Bilirubin, total: 11.3 mg/dL - Bilirubin, direct: 7.8
mg/dL Physical examination reveals yellow/orange skin discoloration, with otherwise normal cardiac,
pulmonary, abdominal, and neurological findings. Which of the following is characteristically associated
with this patient's underlying condition? Answer Choices: (A) Cholestasis with bile duct obstruction (B)
Decreased synthesis of albumin (C) Increased enterohepatic circulation of bilirubin (D) Impaired bile
canalicular transport (E) Increased liver enzymes with AST > ALT (F) Decreased UDP-glucuronyl

transferase activity (G) Accumulation of unconjugated bilirubin (H) Excessive hemolysis of red blood
cells (I) Deposition of copper in hepatic tissues (J) Hyperpigmentation of the liver
 A. Accumulation of unconjugated bilirubin
B. Deposition of copper in hepatic tissues
C. Increased enterohepatic circulation of bilirubin
D. Hyperpigmentation of the liver
E. Excessive hemolysis of red blood cells
F. Increased liver enzymes with AST > ALT
G. Impaired bile canalicular transport
H. Decreased synthesis of albumin
I. Cholestasis with bile duct obstruction
J. Decreased UDP-glucuronyl transferase activity
